author: buremba
body:
## Summary
Closes the identity-graph gap that was blocking gateway routing — the gateway can now resolve "which user owns this WhatsApp JID?" via a single \`entity_identities\` lookup once these rows are populated.

**New file: \`packages/owletto-backend/src/auth/subject-identities.ts\`**
- \`provisionMemberAndCoreIdentities(orgId, subject)\` — creates the user's \`\$member\` entity in the org and writes \`entity_identities\` rows for \`auth_user_id\` and \`email\`. Reuses the existing \`ensureMemberEntity\` helper.
- \`linkWhatsAppToMember({orgId, email, rawPhone})\` — normalizes the user's phone to E.164, derives the WhatsApp JID (\`<digits>@s.whatsapp.net\`), and writes \`phone\` + \`wa_jid\` identity rows. Idempotent.
- \`normalizePhoneE164\` + \`phoneToWhatsAppJid\` pure helpers (covered by 7 unit tests — UK +44 national, leading 0, full E.164, the \`+44 (0) ...\` trunk-prefix form, non-UK numbers).

**Modified: \`personal-org-provisioning.ts\` (signup hook)**
- After creating the org, call \`provisionMemberAndCoreIdentities\` so every signed-up user lands with a \`\$member\` entity in their own org and discoverable identities. Failure is logged, doesn't roll back the org.

**Modified: \`install-routes.ts\` (POST /api/install)**
- Accepts an optional \`whatsapp_phone\` in the body. On valid phone: writes \`wa_jid\` + \`phone\` identities to the user's \`\$member\`. Reports \`whatsappError=\"invalid_phone\"\` or \`\"no_member\"\` without failing the install (agent is in; user can re-link later).

**Integration tests**
- Install with \`whatsapp_phone\` writes both identity rows correctly.
- Install with unparseable phone surfaces \`whatsappError=\"invalid_phone\"\` and still completes.

## Stacked on
Targets \`feat/install-endpoint\` (#357). Pulls in \`feat/personal-org-on-signup\` (#352) via merge so both \`personal-org-provisioning.ts\` and \`install-routes.ts\` are in scope.

⚠️ Both \`feat/personal-org-on-signup\` and \`feat/schema-mirror-install-flow\` have seen upstream refactors after this PR was opened (advisory locks for concurrency; classifier/watcher mirroring). When this branch rebases at merge time it'll need to integrate with the new tips — my additions are confined to a new helper file plus one new call site, so the conflicts should be small and mechanical.

## Test plan
- [x] 7 unit tests for phone normalization + JID derivation.
- [x] 5 integration tests in \`install-routes.test.ts\` (including 2 new ones for the WhatsApp identity path).
- [x] Pre-commit Biome + tsc pass.
- [ ] Manual: \`POST /api/install -d '{"templateAgentId":"...","whatsapp_phone":"+447123456789"}'\` while signed in; confirm \`entity_identities\` rows appear with namespaces \`phone\` and \`wa_jid\`.
- [ ] Manual: re-run the same POST; confirm rows aren't duplicated (idempotent).

## Why this matters
This is the missing link. Before: WhatsApp routing (#7) had nothing to query because no code wrote the JID anywhere. After: every install writes \`wa_jid\` to the right \`\$member\` in the right org, and the gateway routing PR can be a clean \`SELECT organization_id FROM entity_identities WHERE namespace='wa_jid' AND identifier=\$senderJid\`.

author: jabbertones-cloud
body:
Three Sprint-1 follow-ups to the v3.1.0 CADAM ship, derived from a [106-source NotebookLM cross-pollination research pass](https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/4e13f3d9-732b-4d8b-95cb-d172f62cb813) across parametric (CadQuery, Build123d, OpenSCAD, FreeCAD, Solvespace, Manifold), procedural (Geometry Nodes, Sverchok, Houdini HDA, USD), BIM (IfcOpenShell, BlenderBIM/Bonsai, Speckle), and AI-native (Zoo.dev, ahujasid, PatrykIti, blender.org MCP, BlenderGPT, ThreeStudio, LL3M, BlenderGym, Voyager, ReAct, Reflexion, Text2CAD, CADmium, DeepCAD, Cherchi mesh booleans) sources.

## Commits

| SHA | Closes | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `9c7e460` | #11 | docs: full research report, integration plan, GitHub issue specs, SKILL.md append |
| `06bdbf0` | #6 | feat: typed `needs_input` payload for `router_set_goal` + `plan` (apply_params already wired in v3.1.0) |
| `9ab587b` | #10 | refactor: migrate 11 raw `execute_python` sites in `product_animation_tools.py` to CADAM contract; bonus indent-bug fix in `_gen_material_code` |

## What landed

### #11 — docs (commit `9c7e460`)
- `docs/CAD_RESEARCH_REPORT.md` (19K) — repo teardowns + ranked Top-12 features + interop matrix + hard truths
- `docs/CAD_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md` (14K) — how the 12 features fold onto the v3.1.0 CADAM contract (Tier 0–4)
- `docs/CAD_GITHUB_ISSUES.md` (25K) — full issue specs (mirrored to GH issues #1–#12)
- `docs/SKILL_V3_1_0_APPEND.md` — Tier taxonomy + PARAMETERS conventions ready to paste into `.claude/skills/blender-mcp/SKILL.md`
- `scripts/ship-cad-batch.sh` — commit/push helper

### #6 — `needs_input` (commit `06bdbf0`)
Pattern from [`PatrykIti/blender-ai-mcp`](https://github.com/PatrykIti/blender-ai-mcp). When a tool can't proceed because of missing/unknown input, return a typed payload so the calling model can ask the user instead of guessing or regenerating an entire script.

```json
{
  "status": "needs_input",
  "needs_input": {
    "field": "DEPTH",
    "kind": "number",
    "description": "...",
    "default": 2.0,
    "choices": [...]?,
    "available": {...}?,
    "hint": "..."
  }
}
```

Wired into:
- `blender_apply_params` (v3.1.0): unknown override key, empty overrides, PARAMETERS-rewrite failure
- `blender_router_set_goal` (this PR): empty goal, invalid profile
- `blender_plan` (this PR): missing goal

### #10 — product_animation CADAM migration (commit `9ab587b`)
All 11 raw `send_command_fn("execute_python", ...)` call sites in `server/product_animation_tools.py` now route through `run_cadam_script` (added in v3.1.0), giving each site:
- PARAMETERS-block manifest of input args (audit trail)
- Server-side AST gate
- LRU script cache keyed by stable `script_id`
- `blender_apply_params` re-runnability — tweak FOV/energy without re-LLM

`register_product_tools` accepts an optional 4th `run_cadam_script_fn` arg; legacy 3-arg callers continue to work.

**Bonus discovery**: the CADAM AST gate caught a latent indent bug in `_gen_material_code` (join string was 8 spaces vs template's 4) that broke 7/16 material presets. The legacy `execute_python` path silently swallowed the resulting Python `SyntaxError` inside Blender. Now all 16 presets parse cleanly. **First dividend of the v3.1.0 contract.**

## Tests

37 passing tests across 5 self-contained suites, no live Blender required:

| Suite | Tests | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cadam_p1_p2_split_exec.py` | 9 | v3.1.0 base |
| `test_cadam_p3_reference_image.py` | 5 | v3.1.0 base |
| `test_cadam_p4_list_assets.py` | 7 | v3.1.0 base |
| `test_needs_input.py` | 8 | **new** — incl. 3-step `needs_input → answer → needs_input → answer → success` flow |
| `test_product_animation_cadam_migration.py` | 8 | **new** — incl. apply_params round-trip on a product_animation `script_id` |

## How to verify locally

```bash
cd ~/claw-architect/openclaw-blender-mcp
git checkout fix/addon-tool-coverage-2026-04-24
for t in tests/test_cadam_p1_p2_split_exec.py tests/test_cadam_p3_reference_image.py tests/test_cadam_p4_list_assets.py tests/test_needs_input.py tests/test_product_animation_cadam_migration.py; do
  ./.venv/bin/python3.12 "$t"
done
```

## Related

- Closes #6, #10, #11
- Partially closes meta epic #12 (v3.2 roadmap)
- Builds on v3.1.0 ship (commit `00a5dca`)

## Summary

Closes the lint-config cluster. Lands at `golangci-lint run = 0 issues` (was 15 baseline + a config-validation error against the pinned `golangci-lint v2.9.0`).

## Root cause

- `gosec.excludes` listed `G117` and `G704` — neither is a real gosec rule ID, and `golangci-lint v2.9.0` rejects the config outright (see `golangci-lint config verify` output before this PR).
- `bootstrap/summary.go` had a whole-file `errcheck` exclusion to silence `fmt.Fprint*` failures on a configurable writer — the exclusion was too broad and would have hidden any new errcheck issue introduced in that file.

## Fix

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Config | Removed invalid `G117` / `G704` from gosec excludes. Tightened bootstrap-summary errcheck exclusion to `fmt.Fprint*` source pattern only. Added `gofumpt` formatter. |

Replaced `errors.As` (which resolved to local pkg) with `stderrors.As` in `validation/struct_validator.go`. `len(p) == 0` → `p == ""` in `errors/response.go`. body:
## Summary

Pre-Phase-3 audit found four loose ends in the D5 auth work that shipped over PRs #83-#88. Fixing them all here so we move into OIDC with a clean baseline.

## Findings + fixes

### 1. Periodic auth-state sweep was never wired ⚠️
The store had `delete_expired_user_sessions()` (#83) and `delete_expired_link_codes()` (#88), but **nothing called them**. Without this, expired session rows and unconsumed-but-expired link codes accumulate forever.

**Fix:** Added `_sweep_auth_state()` as a startup background task in `src/gluon/web/api.py`, mirroring the existing `_cleanup_old_logs` / `_cleanup_old_worktrees` pattern. Default 1-hour cadence, tunable via `GLUON_AUTH_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS`. Registered for graceful cancellation in the shutdown handler.

### 2. Dead code: `isSystemUser()` export
The function was exported from `web-ui/src/lib/types.ts` but **never imported anywhere** — the one caller that needs the SYSTEM_USER check (`useCurrentUser`) uses the constant directly.

**Fix:** Removed the function, kept the constant with a clearer doc-comment explaining its single purpose.

### 3. Stale "added in a follow-up" comment
`disable_user_endpoint` in api.py had a comment from #84 claiming attribution columns were "added in a follow-up". That follow-up shipped in #85.

**Fix:** Updated the comment to reference the actual columns (`execution_runs.user_id`, `orchestrator_tasks.created_by_user_id`, `pending_approvals.decided_by_user_id`).

### 4. README + CLAUDE.md missing auth docs
README had **zero mention** of `GLUON_AUTH_ENABLED`, the multi-user model, the `/link` self-serve flow, or the dashboard auth UI. Anyone discovering Gluon today wouldn't know multi-user auth exists.

**Fix:**
- README.md gains a new "Multi-User Authentication (Optional)" feature section under Security & Isolation, summarizing all of D5 in one block.
- CLAUDE.md gains a D5 env-vars block and the bootstrap recipe (`gluon user add alice --role admin`) so future onboarding doesn't have to grep the codebase.

## Audit findings I deliberately did NOT touch

| Reported | Reality |
|---|---|
| ALTER TABLE lacks IF NOT EXISTS | False alarm — `store.py:960-964` wraps each migration in try/except `OperationalError`. |
| CLI parity gap | False alarm — full `gluon user *` command surface exists from Phase 1 (`cli.py:5397+`). |
| No bootstrap test | The existing CLI tests cover user creation; not a regression introduced by D5. |

## Test plan

- [x] `bun tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `bun biome check .` — clean
- [x] `bun run build` — clean
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/` — **2054 passed** (1 unrelated teardown error in long-running suite; passes in isolation, predates this change)

body:
## Summary

Release A of the **Vitana ID** initiative: a permanent, globally unique, ASR-friendly user identifier (`@alex3700` style) that becomes the canonical identity primitive across voice commands, support tickets, audit logs, OASIS events, marketplace records, and cross-tenant joins.

This PR is **schema-only**. No gateway code changes. No service reads or writes the new columns. Fully reversible (drop column + trigger).

Plan: `.claude/plans/i-want-a-solution-streamed-patterson.md` (Part 1 / Release A).

## What ships

9 migrations, run individually via `RUN-MIGRATION.yml`, **off-peak** for the backfill:

| # | File | Purpose |
|---|------|---------|
| 1 | `20260427000000_vitana_id_extensions.sql` | `pg_trgm` + `fuzzystrmatch` + `unaccent` |
| 2 | `20260427000100_vitana_id_reserved_table.sql` | `vitana_id_reserved` — reserved-word governance, single source of truth |
| 3 | `20260427000200_vitana_id_generator.sql` | `generate_vitana_id_suggestion()` — alex3700-style; alias-aware uniqueness |
| 4 | `20260427000300_vitana_id_schema.sql` | `profiles.vitana_id` + `vitana_id_locked`; `app_users.vitana_id` mirror column; `handle_aliases` table; trigram index |
| 5 | `20260427000400_vitana_id_mirror_trigger.sql` | One-way mirror `profiles → app_users` (read replica only) |
| 6 | `20260427000500_handle_aliases_backfill.sql` | Preserve every legacy handle for 301 redirects + legacy support lookups |
| 7 | `20260427000600_vitana_id_backfill.sql` | Batched (1000/loop) backfill of every existing profile + replace `handle = vitana_id` + `NOT NULL` + `CHECK` regex |
| 8 | `20260427000700_handle_new_user_replace.sql` | Replaces existing trigger; preserves tenant/membership/role/`active_tenant_id` logic |
| 9 | `20260427000800_resolve_recipient_rpc.sql` | `resolve_recipient_candidates()` — voice resolver primitive (peer + global modes) |

## Architecture decisions (locked)

- **Format**: `<3-6 lowercase chars from given name><4 digits>`. Reserved-word collisions get `u` prefix. Empty/non-Latin → `user`. Suffix escalates to 5 digits, then `user<6digits>`.
- **Canonical data model — Option A**: `profiles.vitana_id` is source of truth. `app_users.vitana_id` is trigger-mirrored. App code MUST NEVER write `app_users.vitana_id` directly.
- **Mutability**: permanent. `vitana_id_locked` flips true once on the onboarding card (Release B) and never resets.
- **Replace policy**: legacy handle column becomes a mirror of `vitana_id`. Old values preserved in `handle_aliases` for redirects.
- **Friend boost (+0.08)** in resolver: deferred to Release B — `relationship_edges` lives gateway-side and the column shape isn't visible from this repo's migrations.

## Backward-compatibility contracts (invariants for ALL releases)

1. Identifier normalization — resolver treats `@foo` ≡ `foo`.
2. No self-resolution — `WHERE user_id <> p_actor` (matches `chat.ts:46` self-send block).
3. Null-tolerant writers (Release B will rely on this; nothing writes `vitana_id` from app code in Release A).
4. Fallback display — frontend shows `display_name`/`handle` if `vitana_id` is null. Never crashes on null.
5. Trigger-only mirror — `app_users.vitana_id` updated only by `profiles_vitana_id_mirror_trigger`.
6. Alias preservation — `handle_aliases` is append-only.
7. Reserved-word grandfathering — existing holders never forced to rename.

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply migrations 1-9 sequentially via `RUN-MIGRATION.yml` on staging
- [ ] After each migration, verify schema with `psql ... -c "\d+ public.profiles"` / `\d+ public.app_users` / `\dt public.handle_aliases public.vitana_id_reserved`
- [ ] After backfill (migration 7): `SELECT count(*) FROM profiles WHERE vitana_id IS NULL` → 0
- [ ] After backfill: `SELECT count(*) FROM app_users WHERE vitana_id IS NULL AND user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM profiles)` → 0 (mirror trigger fired)
- [ ] After backfill: `SELECT vitana_id, count(*) FROM profiles GROUP BY vitana_id HAVING count(*) > 1` → 0 rows
- [ ] After backfill: `SELECT count(*) FROM handle_aliases` → matches non-null legacy handle count
- [ ] Resolver smoke test: `SELECT * FROM resolve_recipient_candidates('<actor_uuid>', '@daniela', 5, false)` returns ranked candidates
- [ ] Generator smoke test: `SELECT generate_vitana_id_suggestion('Dragan Alexander', 'Dragan Alexander', 'd@example.com')` → matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9]{3,11}$`
- [ ] Reserved-word reject: `SELECT generate_vitana_id_suggestion('admin', 'admin', 'a@x.com')` → does NOT start with `admin` (gets `u` prefix → `uadmin####`)
- [ ] Handle_new_user trigger smoke: create a test signup, verify profile + global_community_profile + memberships + role_preferences + active_tenant_id all populated as before, plus new vitana_id

## Rollback

Each migration is reversible in reverse order. If anything goes wrong, abort before merging Release B.

## Next

- **Release B**: gateway middleware (`req.identity.vitanaId`), `/auth/me` extension, resolver endpoint, ORB voice tools (`resolve_recipient`, `send_chat_message`, `share_link`), onboarding pick UX, alias-redirect router on frontend.
- **Release C**: enforcement, cross-system tagging audit, Command Hub admin views.
- **Part 2**: reverse marketplace.

## Summary
Reviewer's follow-up on #431. The validator handled \`..\` and absolute paths but \`PurePosixPath\` silently collapses dot segments before the parts check ran, so \`'.'\`, \`'./'\`, \`'./.'\`, \`'a/./b'\`, and \`'weights/.'\` slipped through. The collapsed path resolved to \`dest_dir\` itself, and \`_digest_matches\` then opened the directory and raised \`IsADirectoryError\` instead of the expected \`OctomilError(INVALID_INPUT)\`.

Fix: split on \`/\` before normalization and reject any segment in \`{'', '.', '..'}\`. Keep the post-normalization check as defense in depth.

author: kalujo
body:
## What the user said
> no the artifacts happen here. when i go to prompt 67 you can see that the wrapping of the text is broken thus overflowing and breaking it overall

The screenshot showed it clearly: the \"artifacts\" weren't ghost frames at all — they were the actual prompt text, which contained a markdown comparison table. The tabs in that table were making ratatui's `Paragraph` + `Wrap { trim: false }` miscount column width by 7 per `\t`, so the wrap drifted off and spilled into mid-word fragments at the right edge.

## Fix
Pre-process every line of `d.prompt_text` and `d.response_text` through `sanitize_for_display` before handing it to `Paragraph`:

| input | what we do |
|---|---|
| `\t` | expand to 4 spaces |
| `ESC [ … final` (CSI: SGR, cursor moves) | strip the whole sequence |
| `ESC ] … BEL` / `… ESC \\` (OSC: titles, hyperlinks) | strip the whole sequence |
| `\r`, `\u{0b}`, `\u{0c}`, `\0`, other control chars | drop |
| everything else | passthrough unchanged |

After sanitization every char in a line occupies exactly its character-count's worth of display columns, so the wrap math agrees with the actual rendered width and no overflow happens.

The earlier `Clear` defenses (frame-level + detail-pane-inner) stay in — they're cheap insurance for the genuinely-stale-cell case if it ever comes up.

## Tests
6 new unit tests cover tab expansion, SGR + cursor-move stripping, CR / FF / VT cleanup, bare control-char removal, and a realistic markdown-table row from the user's actual draft. 105 tests pass total, clippy + fmt clean, release green.

author: apherwani
body:
## Summary

The Create Room button felt unresponsive — sometimes requiring multiple taps. Two causes:

1. **Wasted round trip.** The flow was `POST /api/rooms` → WebSocket handshake → `create-room` → `room-created`, three sequential network calls before navigation. The `/api/rooms` endpoint did nothing but generate a random 4-char code; we can do that on-device for free.
2. **Multi-tap cancellation.** The button had no `disabled` state during the in-flight request. Each repeat tap regenerated `pendingRoomCode`, which made `useWebSocket` close the in-flight socket and reopen against a new code — actively aborting the create that was about to succeed. The user's "sometimes I need to tap multiple times" was the bug compounding itself.

Fixed by:
- Generating the room code client-side (drops one round trip).
- Adding a `busy` flag that disables both Create and Join buttons during the request and swaps the label to "Creating room…" / "Joining room…". Resets on any server error.
- Server-side `handleCreateRoom` now rejects when `this.initialized` is already true. With on-device code generation collisions are theoretically possible (~0.03% with 24⁴ codes), and with the persistence layer added in #17 a collision would silently overwrite an active room. Tapping Create again regenerates a fresh code and retries.

Bumped `0.4.1 → 0.4.2`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Tap Create Room once on a slow connection — button should immediately show "Creating room…" and become disabled, even before the WS handshake completes.
- [ ] Spam-tap Create Room — only the first tap registers; subsequent taps are no-ops while busy.
- [ ] Create succeeds and lands in the lobby as before.
- [ ] Create with empty name (digital mode) — button stays disabled, no tap registers.
- [ ] Same checks for Join Room.
- [ ] If a server error comes back (e.g. simulated by hand-crafting a colliding code in two browser tabs), the busy state clears and the user can tap again.

body: ## Summary Fix-forward de 2 issues 🔴 críticos que o Devin Review pegou no PR #15 *após* o merge. ### 1. `enqueue_ocr_parte_diaria` vazava conexões do broker `Celery(broker=...)` aloca pool TCP interno (Redis/AMQP) que nunca era fechado. Como a função é chamada em **todo upload** (`POST /partes-diarias`) e **todo reprocessar** (`POST /{id}/reprocessar`), cada request vazava ~1 conexão Redis. Em produção com volume, esgota o pool em poucas horas. **Fix:** `_celery_dispatcher_singleton` em `service.py` + `get_celery_dispatcher()` lazy + `reset_celery_dispatcher_singleton()` chamado no `lifespan` shutdown de `main.py`. Mesmo padrão dos outros singletons (`Infosimples`, `Dominio`, `DocumentAI`). ### 2. Worker ignorava `STORAGE_BACKEND=onedrive` `_run_ocr_parte_diaria` no worker construía `LocalStorage` direto, mas o router da API respeita `STORAGE_BACKEND` e usa `OneDriveStorage` quando configurado. Resultado: API salvava com item_id do Graph no DB, worker chamava `LocalStorage.read(item_id)` → `FileNotFoundError` sempre. **OCR nunca rodaria em deploy com OneDrive.** **Fix:** extraído helper compartilhado `open_partes_diarias_storage(settings)` em `service.py` (async context manager — fecha o `httpx.AsyncClient` do OneDrive no `finally`). Tanto `router.get_partes_diarias_storage` quanto o worker `_run_ocr_parte_diaria` agora usam o mesmo helper. Sem possibilidade de divergência. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Confirmar que o lifespan do FastAPI continua subindo sem erro (verificar logs de startup local: `docker compose up api`) - [ ] Quando ligar OneDrive em prod (`STORAGE_BACKEND=onedrive` + credenciais reais Microsoft Graph), validar end-to-end: upload de parte diária pela UI → worker lê o anexo do OneDrive (não do disco) → status vira `processado` - [ ] (Opcional, observabilidade) Em staging, verificar que `redis-cli CLIENT LIST` não cresce indefinidamente conforme uploads acontecem ### Notes - 278 testes passando (+3 regressão: singleton da `Celery`, helper local, helper OneDrive com `aclose` garantido) - `ruff` (api + workers) + `eslint` verdes - Adicionado `apps/workers/.gitignore` para não vazar `uv.lock` em commits futuros (mesma decisão do `apps/api/.gitignore`) - Devin Review marcou como 🔴 ambos. Ainda há 9 findings adicionais no review da PR #15 (link no thread); posso atacar em PR separado se você quiser, mas a maioria parece estilística — vou ler e me posicionar antes Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/1c17171b07f94afdb601f97213a8a29d Requested by: @paraisolorrayne ---

author: dgraciac
body:
## Summary

Adds a single workflow (\`.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml\`) that flips \`--auto\` merge on PRs opened by \`dependabot[bot]\` when the bump is non-major AND the dependency is a devDep. Major bumps and any runtime-dependency change still wait for a human reviewer.

## Mechanics

- Trigger: \`pull_request\` to \`main\`.
- Step 1: \`dependabot/fetch-metadata@v2\` reads \`update-type\` and \`dependency-type\`.
- Step 2: if \`(update-type != version-update:semver-major) && (dependency-type == direct:development)\` → \`gh pr merge --auto --squash\`.

\`--auto\` only schedules the merge; GitHub still gates it on every required status check (CI, CodeQL, Chromatic). **The workflow cannot bypass branch protection** — if checks fail, no merge happens.

## Coverage

| Dependabot PR shape | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| devDep, patch | auto-merged when checks pass |
| devDep, minor | auto-merged when checks pass |
| devDep, major | left open for human review |
| runtime dep, any bump | left open for human review |

## Required one-off setup (outside this PR)

- Repo setting **"Allow auto-merge"** must be enabled (\`gh api PATCH repos/code-sherpas/pharos-react -f allow_auto_merge=true\`). Done in a follow-up step.
- Any secret used by a workflow that runs on Dependabot PRs must also exist as a **Dependabot secret** (Actions secrets are not exposed to Dependabot's restricted token). Today: \`CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN\` — already replicated.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green.
- [ ] After merge + allow_auto_merge enabled, the next devDep patch/minor opened by Dependabot gets auto-merged when its checks turn green.
- [ ] A simulated major-bump PR (or any runtime dep) stays open.

## Related

Companion PR in \`pharos-tokens\` lands the same workflow there.

body:
## Summary

Three independent fixes scoped to the HyDE/RAG pipeline, all uncovered while debugging a real session.

- **OpenAI native dimension by model.** `llm/embedding/openai.go` no longer uses a single hardcoded 1536 default. New helper `openaiNativeDim(model)` resolves to 1536 for `text-embedding-3-small` and `text-embedding-ada-002`, 3072 for `text-embedding-3-large`. The `Embed` gate on the request `dimensions` field also compares against this per-model native, so Matryoshka truncation via `CHATCLI_EMBED_DIMENSIONS` keeps working unchanged.
- **Lazy backfill cap raised from 25 to 500** in `cli/workspace/memory/store.go`. Comment refreshed with the actual cost estimate at Voyage pricing — about US\$0.001 for a fully cold cache of 500 facts. Users with hundreds of facts now get cosine coverage on the first interaction instead of being stuck at 25 forever.
- **Removed dead `CHATCLI_QUALITY_HYDE_PROVIDER` env var** and the `EmbedProvider` field on `HyDEConfig`. It only annotated the `/config quality` display and never wired the embedding factory — a silent footgun where users would see the chosen backend in the UI while the actual provider fell back to null. `CHATCLI_EMBED_PROVIDER` is now the single source of truth, and the doc-comment on `HyDEConfig` records why the field was removed.

## Bug it fixes (with timeline)

A user setting `CHATCLI_EMBED_MODEL=text-embedding-3-large` without `CHATCLI_EMBED_DIMENSIONS` would hit:

```
HyDE vector index attached  provider=openai:text-embedding-3-large  dimension=1536
vector backfill failed: provider openai:text-embedding-3-large emitted dim=3072
                       but store dim=1536 (clear ... to migrate)
```

The provider declared 1536 from the global constant, the API returned the model's native 3072, and the store rejected every single backfill. After this PR the same env yields a 3072-dim store and clean backfills.

## Files

- `llm/embedding/openai.go` — added `openaiNativeDim`, removed `openaiDefaultDim`, updated `NewOpenAI` and `Embed`
- `cli/workspace/memory/store.go` — backfill cap 25 → 500 with refreshed comment
- `cli/agent/quality/config.go` — removed `EmbedProvider` field, removed env loader for `CHATCLI_QUALITY_HYDE_PROVIDER`, doc-comment on `HyDEConfig` explains the removal
- `cli/config_quality.go` — removed display row for the dead var
- `docs/SEVEN_PATTERNS_PLAN.md` — struct doc updated to match

## Test plan

- [x] \`go build ./...\` clean
- [x] \`go test ./...\` — full suite green, including \`llm/embedding\`, \`cli/agent/quality\`, \`cli/workspace/memory\`
- [x] Manual: set \`CHATCLI_EMBED_MODEL=text-embedding-3-large\` without \`CHATCLI_EMBED_DIMENSIONS\`, confirm vector index attaches at dim=3072 and backfill succeeds
- [x] Manual: confirm \`/config quality\` no longer shows the \`CHATCLI_QUALITY_HYDE_PROVIDER\` line
- [x] Manual: with hundreds of facts, confirm \`vector_count\` in \`/config quality\` rises beyond 25 after a single retrieve

## Doc companion

Documentation in \`~/chatcli.ai\` (separate repo) was updated and pushed in commit \`2b86d3f\` to keep \`features/quality/rag-hyde.mdx\`, \`features/quality/configuration.mdx\` and \`reference/environment-variables.mdx\` (PT + EN) consistent with this change.

The `sanitize_text` function was identified as a bottleneck in the hot path of the scanner (processing model names and server responses). By adding fast-path guards, we avoid the overhead of `re.sub()` for strings that don't require sanitization.

Improvements:
- Added `'\x1b' in text` check to skip ANSI escape cleanup for most strings.
- Added `NON_PRINTABLE.search(text)` check to skip control character cleanup.
- Fixed minor linting issues (E302, E501) in both scanner scripts.
- Verified that sequential checks are more efficient than a single combined regex alternation.
- Documented findings in `.jules/bolt.md`.

Benchmarked performance on 200,000 iterations:
- Short clean strings: +88% faster
- Long clean strings: +15% faster
- Strings requiring cleanup: negligible overhead (+7% for ANSI, -2% for control chars)

body:
## Summary
- New `_looks_like_goodbye(reply)` helper recognises wrap-up phrases ("your order is in", "have it ready", "see you soon", "thanks for calling", etc.) and rejects replies still ending with `?`.
- Auto-hangup mark now fires when EITHER:
  - `state.order.status == CONFIRMED` (the explicit prompt path from #78), OR
  - `is_ready_to_confirm()` AND `status != CANCELLED` AND `_looks_like_goodbye(full_reply)` — the safety net.
- When the fallback fires, the status flip is mirrored locally so the `finally`-block `persist_on_confirm` sees it.
- Prompt nudge: adds a CRITICAL directive coupling goodbye phrases with the `status="confirmed"` tool call.
- 4 new tests. 104/104 backend tests pass.

## Why
Live call `CA9c2679ab4e619d5ea50fbe599f9eb501` (2026-04-26 01:46): Haiku said *"Great, your order is in — we'll have it ready for you soon!"* but didn't call `update_order(status="confirmed")`. `state.order.status` stayed `IN_PROGRESS`, the auto-hangup mark never fired, and the call hung for 16 seconds until the caller manually disconnected. Order was confirmed only by the `finally`-block persist on WebSocket close.

## Linked issue
Closes #84.

(Branch is named `fix/79-…` from a numbering mistake when I created the fix before the issue. Issue #79 is a different Sprint 2.1 epic — ignore the branch number.)

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest -v` — 104/104 (100 prior + 4 new on the heuristic + prompt directive).
- [ ] Live test 1: place a pickup order and confirm. After bot says "your order is in", ~3s of silence, call ends.
- [ ] Live test 2: confirm the order, then immediately ask a follow-up. Call should NOT drop; conversation continues.
- [ ] Live test 3: bot mid-conversation says "One large margarita, got it. What size?" — must NOT trigger fallback (ends with `?`).

## Notes
- Heuristic is intentionally conservative — phrase list + `is_ready_to_confirm()` + no trailing `?`. If Haiku regularly bypasses the prompt, we tighten further; if false positives appear, drop the looser phrases.
- The prompt's CRITICAL framing is the long-term reliable path — the fallback exists so a single missed tool call doesn't degrade the caller experience for 30 seconds.

body:
## Summary

Closes the top 5 findings from the 2026-04-25 modernization audit
(`claudedocs/modernization-audit-2026-04-25.md`). Each commit is atomic
and self-contained — review per commit.

| # | Finding | Severity | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | Global request body size cap (RFC 9457 413) | 🟡 | `924de2b4` |
| 6 | Zod-validate JSONB write boundaries on runs + run_logs | 🟡 | `e2b6dbd0` |
| 3 | Durable `audit_events` table + `recordAudit` helper | 🔴 | `481cf96f` |
| 1 | Consumer-lockstep CI gate before `@appstrate/core` publish | 🔴 | `e32b8e75` |
| 2 | Versioned BETTER_AUTH secrets with online rotation window | 🔴 | `3c585bb2` |

Theme: **audit-readiness & operational rotation** — the SOC2-shaped
gaps (audit trail, secret rotation, body limits, JSONB validation) plus
the consumer-version drift that blocks any other cross-repo work.

## What ships

### #9 — Global body limit
- New env var `API_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` (default 10 MB).
- New `payloadTooLarge()` helper in `@appstrate/core/api-errors` so
  413s flow through the central problem+json error handler.
- New `apps/api/src/middleware/body-limit.ts` Hono middleware applied
  globally; skipped for `/api/uploads/_content` (signed-token PUT).

### #6 — JSONB Zod schemas
- `runMetadataSchema` (8 KB) / `runConfigSchema` (16 KB) / `runLogDataSchema` (32 KB).
- Strict reject on `runs.metadata` and `runs.config` writes (400).
- Best-effort drop on `run_logs.data` (high-volume path; logs and
  drops the field, the surrounding event still ingests).
- `$type<Record<string, unknown>>` on `run_logs.data` for read-side
  type safety.

### #3 — `audit_events` table
- New schema + migration `0012_audit_events.sql`.
- `recordAudit()` (best-effort, never throws) + `recordAuditFromContext()`
  (derives actor/IP/UA/request-id from Hono context).
- Wired from API keys (create + revoke) and connections (create +
  delete) — the two highest-stakes mutation surfaces. Other paths can
  be added later without API churn.

### #1 — Core consumer lockstep
- `scripts/check-consumer-versions.ts` — fetches `package.json` from
  every known consumer (registry, cloud, portal) via the GitHub API
  and compares the pinned `^X.Y.Z` range to the version about to be
  published.
- Drift policy: ≥ 2 minors behind → fail (block publish), 1 minor →
  warn, in sync → OK.
- Wired into `publish-core.yml` after the tag-vs-package.json check,
  before npm publish.
- Override via `CONSUMER_DRIFT_POLICY=warn|off` repo variable for
  emergency hotfixes.

### #2 — Versioned auth secrets
- New env vars `BETTER_AUTH_SECRETS` (`{ kid: secret }` JSON map) and
  `BETTER_AUTH_ACTIVE_KID` (defaults to `k1`).
- New `apps/api/src/lib/auth-secrets.ts`: `getActiveAuthSecret()`,
  `signAuthHmac()`, `verifyAuthHmac()`.
- `pending-client-cookie.ts` migrated as the first consumer.
- Backward compat: when `BETTER_AUTH_SECRETS` is empty (default), the
  helper derives `{ [active]: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET }` so existing
  deployments keep working unchanged.
- The legacy un-prefixed signature format is still accepted for
  rolling out the helper without invalidating in-flight cookies.

**Known limit**: Better Auth itself does not yet accept a verification
list, so rotating the session cookie still requires re-login. The env
wiring is now in place for any future plugin-side dual-key support, and
every HMAC the platform owns can rotate online.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run check` (turbo typecheck + lint + format + verify-openapi + detect-breaking)
- [x] `bun test apps/api/test/unit/` (703 pass, 0 fail)
- [x] New `auth-secrets.test.ts` (9 tests covering legacy + rotation paths)
- [x] OIDC `signup-guard.test.ts` continues to pass (legacy un-prefixed cookie format)
- [ ] CI: full integration suite + e2e

## Out of scope (deferred, not blocked by this PR)
- Wiring `recordAudit()` into agents / schedules / webhooks / applications
  (additive, no API churn).
- Better Auth plugin for session-cookie multi-secret verification
  (requires upstream cooperation).
- Audit-events admin endpoint (`GET /api/audit-events`).
- Bumping `@appstrate/core` ranges in registry/cloud/portal (those repo
  PRs are out of `appstrate/`'s scope per audit guardrails — but the
  CI gate this PR adds will require them at the next core publish).

author: aki1770-del
body:
## What this PR does

Two changes shipped together because the second is the first user of the first.

### 1. Loom Protocol extension — `propose_patch(self, finding, repo_root)`

`Loom.propose_patch` now takes a second positional argument: the absolute path to the repo root the loom scanned. Looms that **modify** an existing file (read-merge-emit) need to read that file at patch-compose time. Looms that always **create** a new file (most loom classes today) can ignore it.

Reading from `repo_root` is permitted; **writing remains forbidden** — disk writes are restricted to the CLI `--apply` path per `promises.md` Promise 4.

All four pre-existing looms updated to accept the new signature (their bodies are unchanged — they ignore `repo_root`).

### 2. EofNewlineLoom (V15 poka-yoke)

First user of the extended Protocol. Detects the common case where a maintainer **has** a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (or `.yml`) but did NOT include the `end-of-file-fixer` hook. Reads the existing config from disk, appends the hook block, returns merged contents.

Distinct from `PreCommitFormatterLoom`: that loom handles \"no pre-commit-config at all\"; this loom handles \"config exists but lacks one specific hook.\"

**3-slot vision attribution**:
- `sakichi_vision_id = 15` (poka-yoke — the failure mode this catches)
- `method_vision_ids = [77, 18, 99]` (genchi-genbutsu, 5-Whys, write-it-down — HOW the loom works)
- `stance_vision_ids = [22, 25, 32, 100]` (loom-serves-weaver, autonomation-as-liberation, katei-teki, equal-dignity — HOW the maintainer is treated)

## Why combined

The Protocol extension is enabling infra; without it, EofNewlineLoom can't read the existing config to merge. Shipping them separately would have left the Protocol change without a live consumer in main, hiding a design bug if one existed. EofNewlineLoom is the genchi-genbutsu (V77) for the Protocol shape.

## Test coverage

author: servathadi
body:
## Summary

Self-contained Astro component that emits the meta tags academic indexers expect:

- **citation_*** — Highwire Press tags (what Google Scholar reads)
- **DC.*** — Dublin Core (what other academic indexers read)
- **JSON-LD ScholarlyArticle** — schema.org for general SEO

## Why

Without these tags, Google Scholar will not index a research site's papers, even if the content is otherwise discoverable. This is the primary discoverability surface for the academic audience — most cited papers in physics + foundations get found via Scholar, not direct nav.

Refs #49 (P-010). Discovered onboarding fractalresonance.com onto Inkwell — the corpus is 11 papers + DOIs + Zenodo deposits, and zero of them would surface in Scholar today.

## Usage

In a paper page layout:

\`\`\`astro
import ScholarMeta from '../../components/ScholarMeta.astro'

<ScholarMeta
  paper={{
    title: fm.title,
    authors: fm.authors,
    abstract: fm.abstract,
    doi: fm.doi,
    publishedDate: fm.publishedDate ?? fm.date,
    keywords: fm.keywords,
    series: fm.series,
    id: paper.id,
    language: fm.lang,
  }}
  canonicalUrl={canonicalUrl}
  publisherName={config.name}
/>
\`\`\`

The component is purely presentational — emits meta tags + JSON-LD only, no UI surface. Forks that don't have a research collection ignore it.

## Test plan

- [x] Component renders against the FRC fork's papers schema (verified on FRC-100-007)
- [x] Build passes with the component wired in (\`npm run build\`, 30 pages, zero errors)
- [x] Verified emitted HTML contains:

  - 10 \`DC.*\` tags (title, creator, description, date, type, format, identifier, identifier.doi, language, publisher)
  - JSON-LD \`ScholarlyArticle\` with author, datePublished, identifier, sameAs (DOI URL), publisher, isPartOf

author: tamnd
body:
## Summary

Every AST node had `EndLineno = Lineno` and `EndColOffset = ColOffset` — a zero-width caret that's useless for any tool that wants to underline a span. v0.1.6 starts populating real spans.

- Add `EndPos plexer.Position` to every grammar struct that carries `Pos plexer.Position` (participle populates it automatically).
- Add `ast.spanPos(start, end plexer.Position) Pos` emitter helper.
- Switch every emit site whose AST node maps 1:1 to a participle struct to use `spanPos`.

Synthesized AST nodes (implicit `Tuple` wrapping `return 1, 2`, the `*` `Alias` for `from x import *`, the inner `Name` of a `NamedExpr`, etc.) keep using `pos()`; their union-of-children spans land in v0.1.7+. The CHANGELOG lists every deferred site.

The end positions come from participle (the start of the token immediately after the construct), not CPython's "end_col_offset points past the last character" semantics. Not byte-exact, but a real span. True CPython-faithful end positions need a hand-written parser — that's a v0.2.x problem.

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

Brings BMAD's IDE/agent platform support up to parity with the Vercel skills ecosystem (42 platforms total) and rewrites the install/cleanup model so platforms that share `.agents/skills/` (and other cross-tool standards) coordinate correctly.

### Platforms

- **Existing 24 platforms** rewritten against verified primary docs (commit `5ff534df`):
  - 14 platforms moved to the cross-tool `.agents/skills/` standard (auggie, codex, crush, cursor, gemini, github-copilot, kilo, kimi-code, opencode, pi, roo, rovo-dev, windsurf)
  - Junie fixed (was writing to `.agents/skills/`, which JetBrains never scanned — now writes to `.junie/skills/`)
  - `global_target_dir` added to every platform (XDG for Crush; tool-specific for Codex; shared `~/.agents/skills/` for 11 platforms)
- **18 new platforms added** (commit `6e287245`): adal, amp, bob, command-code, cortex, droid, firebender, goose, kode, mistral-vibe, mux, neovate, openclaw, openhands, pochi, replit, warp, zencoder
- **Preferred set expanded** to: claude-code, cursor, codex, github-copilot

### Coordination for shared `target_dir`

- `IdeManager.setupBatch` dedups skill writes when multiple selected platforms point at the same dir. The first platform writes; peers skip the redundant wipe-and-rewrite. The install summary reports the same count and target dir for every member, e.g. `cursor (56 skills → .agents/skills)` / `gemini (56 skills → .agents/skills)`.
- `IdeManager.cleanupByList` accepts a `remainingIdes` list. Removing one platform from a shared dir while another co-installed platform still owns it skips the directory wipe. Platform-specific hooks (copilot markers, kilo modes, rovodev prompts) still run.
- `_setupIdes` and `_removeDeselectedIdes` updated to use the new batched APIs.

### Skill ownership uses the manifest, not a prefix

`detect()`, `findAncestorConflict()`, and `legacy-warnings.findStaleLegacyDirs()` now read canonicalIds from `_bmad/_config/skill-manifest.csv` rather than matching on the `bmad-` prefix. This unblocks custom modules that ship skills with non-bmad names (e.g. `fred-cool-skill`). The prefix match remains as a documented fallback for the rare case where no manifest is reachable.

### Migration warnings

`LEGACY_SKILL_PATHS` adds 12 dirs that moved to `.agents/skills/` (cursor, gemini, github-copilot, kimi, opencode, pi, roo, rovodev, windsurf, plus their globals). Users with stale skills there get a one-line warning per dir with the `rm` command.

## Files

- `tools/installer/ide/platform-codes.yaml` — 42 platforms verified against primary docs
- `tools/installer/ide/manager.js` — `setupBatch` (new), `cleanupByList` (extended)
- `tools/installer/ide/_config-driven.js` — `detect`/`findAncestorConflict` use canonicalIds; `setup`/`cleanup` honor `skipTarget`
- `tools/installer/ide/shared/installed-skills.js` — `getInstalledCanonicalIds()` + `isBmadOwnedEntry()` helpers (new)
- `tools/installer/core/installer.js` — wires `_setupIdes` to `setupBatch`, `_removeDeselectedIdes` to `cleanupByList(remainingIdes)`
- `tools/installer/core/legacy-warnings.js` — split into command/skill paths, uses canonicalIds
- `test/test-installation-components.js` — Suite 40 (shared-target coordination) and Suite 41 (custom-module skill ownership), 9 new assertions

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:channels` — 83 tests pass
- [x] `npm run test:refs` — 7 tests pass
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean

author: n-ichimura
body:
## Summary

Closing nit from the StorageProvider contract review. `saveImage`
took its data as `Omit<ImageRecord, "path"> & { filename?: string }`
— a side-band `filename` field stitched onto the record that was
not actually part of an `ImageRecord`. The intersection type
worked but mixed two unrelated concerns.

## New shape

```ts
saveImage(
  record: Omit<ImageRecord, "path">,
  opts?: { filename?: string },
): Promise<string>;
```

The record is just `Omit<ImageRecord, "path">` (no filename
contamination). `filename` lives on a dedicated `opts` argument
so its optionality is local to the call site.

## Migration

| Layer | Sites updated |
|---|---|
| 4 `StorageProvider` implementations | Browser / Device / GitHub / Drive |
| Extension mirror | `idb-store.saveImage` + bridge proxy + service-worker dispatcher (`msg.data` + `msg.opts`) |
| Web callers | `capture-host.ts` (timed-capture + file-import), `extension-transfer-host.ts` (bulk transfer), `split-editor-host.ts` (per-page slice) |
| Test helpers | `contract.test-helpers.ts` adds `savePayload(store, payload)`; `file-manager.test.ts` adds `saveTestRecord(store, payload)`; both destructure `filename` off the inline payload before calling. `MemoryStore` test stub gets the new `(record, opts?)` signature. |

The other web callers (`capture-host.ts` paste-from-clipboard /
data-URL save, `extension-transfer-host.ts` single record,
`app.ts` cross-storage save) never passed `filename` — they
work as-is under the new single-arg call shape.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -r typecheck` — all 6 packages green
- [x] `pnpm vitest run` — 41 files / 590 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 findings
- [x] `pnpm --filter @ingcreators/annot-web build`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @ingcreators/annot-extension build`
- [x] All 4 contract tests pass — every backend honours the new
      `(record, opts?)` shape

## Notes

This finishes the StorageProvider contract review the user asked
for after proposal 4 wrapped. With the previous PRs (#149 capability
narrowing + `generateThumbnail` removal, #150 `updateImage` /
`moveImage` split), the contract is now:

- 13 required methods covering image + folder CRUD
- 5 capability interfaces (`Resync`, `ForceRefresh`,
  `TokenRefresher`, `Init`, `RateLimit`) with `supports*`
  predicates
- No semantic overload, no side-band fields, no dead methods

author: avergara13
body:
## Summary
- The price-extraction regex in the "mark as sold" shortcut has two capture groups (`\$(...)` for `$25.00` form, `\bfor\s+(...)\b` for `for 25.00` form), but the previous code read only `?.[1]`. So inputs like "mark X as sold for 25" (no `$`) populated group 2, left group 1 undefined, and the shortcut silently fell through to the LLM despite a valid price.
- Compounded by [#196](https://github.com/avergara13/resale-scanner-pro/pull/196)'s hardening which added a `priceMatch` truthy guard before the destructive `onMarkAsSold` call: post-hardening, *every* no-`$` price command would miss the shortcut entirely.
- Spotted by Copilot's post-merge review of [#196](https://github.com/avergara13/resale-scanner-pro/pull/196).

## Technical Detail
- `src/components/screens/AgentScreen.tsx:1113` — capture the match result into `soldPriceMatch` once, then read `?.[1] || ?.[2]`. Removed the dead-code fallback `text.match(...)?.[1]` that was identical to the first half. Added a comment explaining the alternation semantics so the next person reading this doesn't reintroduce the same bug.

## Test Plan
Browser-verified the regex extraction logic against all four input shapes:

- [x] `"mark X as sold for $25.00"` → `25.00` (group 1)
- [x] `"mark X as sold for 25"` → `25` (group 2, **previously broken**)
- [x] `"mark X as sold $30"` → `30` (group 1)
- [x] `"mark sold ebay for 12.50"` → `12.50` (group 2, **previously broken**)
- [ ] Live agent flow: with an active session that has a published listing, type "mark X as sold for 25" → matches the published item, marks it sold for $25 on the resolved marketplace, message confirms.

## Risk & Rollback
**Risk:** Low — single-line behavioral fix, regex unchanged, only adds the missing group-2 read. tsc + lint clean.
**Rollback:** `git revert <sha>` on main → CI redeploys in ~2 min.

author: effortlesssteven
body:
### Motivation
- The `adze init` scaffold used stale dependency lines (`0.5.0-beta`) and produced projects that often failed to build for new users.  
- First-run scaffolds should be truthful and immediately useful so new users are not blocked by experimental internals.  
- `adze parse` previously implied functionality that is not implemented and produced confusing failures instead of explicit guidance.  

### Description
- Make `adze init` generate a buildable starter crate by producing a minimal, compile-safe `src/grammar.rs` placeholder, a non-invasive `build.rs` scaffold, and a simple compile-time test instead of a snapshot placeholder (`cli/src/main.rs`).  
- Source dependency lines in the generated `Cargo.toml` now prefer local path dependencies when an Adze workspace is detected and otherwise emit git-pinned dependency entries derived from the CLI version tag (via `released_version` and `discover_local_adze_paths`) instead of hardcoded beta versions.  
- Make `adze parse` explicit and truthful: static parse mode now returns a clear unimplemented/experimental error, non-dynamic invocation explains the feature flag requirement, and dynamic mode (when enabled) confirms symbol loading but then reports parser execution as experimental (no silent/mysterious failures).  
- Add integration tests that exercise the first-run path and parse messaging by verifying that `adze init` creates a crate that `cargo check`s and that `adze parse` static mode fails with an explicit experimental message (`cli/tests/cli_test.rs`).  
- Update test fixture version pins from `0.6.0` to `0.8.0` in `test-cli/tree-sitter-mylang/Cargo.toml` to match current workspace lines.  

### Testing

author: yicong-huang
body:
### What changes were proposed in this PR?

`ResumeHandler.resumeWorkflow` (`ResumeHandler.scala`) finished by sending `ExecutionStatsUpdate` and `RuntimeStatisticsPersist` to the client but never sent `ExecutionStateUpdate`. `PauseHandler.scala:88-90` emits the corresponding state event at the end of pause, so the asymmetry meant clients (and tests) had no event-driven signal for the resume → RUNNING transition.

The aggregated state is already correct on the server side after the per-worker resume futures resolve (each `workerInterface.resumeWorker(...)` returns a `WorkerStateResponse` and `ResumeHandler` updates the internal `WorkerExecution` state with that result, so `cp.workflowExecution.getState` returns `RUNNING`). The fix is to broadcast it:

```diff
 sendToClient(ExecutionStatsUpdate(stats))
 sendToClient(RuntimeStatisticsPersist(stats))
+sendToClient(ExecutionStateUpdate(cp.workflowExecution.getState))
```

### Any related issues, documentation, discussions?

Closes #4514

### How was this PR tested?

`sbt WorkflowExecutionService/compile` succeeds; `scalafmtCheckAll` clean. The two existing consumers of `ExecutionStateUpdate` (`ExecutionStatsService.scala:209` and `ExecutionConsoleService.scala:204`) already handle `WorkflowAggregatedState.Recognized`, so an additional `RUNNING` emit at resume time is a strictly additive event. No existing test asserts the absence of this event. Relying on CI for the full backend test run.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Premium tier T9.D — adds an application-level fraud / risk scoring engine plus an admin review surface for moderating flagged applications. Backend-only behavior (no Stripe, no external creds, no new third-party integrations); frontend is a thin admin list page that follows the existing T7.D admin pattern. ### What it does - New `FraudService` (`apps/api/src/fraud/fraud.service.ts`) computes a 0–100 heuristic risk score on each newly-created application from seven signals: - `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL` — trainer email domain matches the curated disposable list (`disposable-domains.ts`, ~50 of the most common throwaway providers). - `HIGH_VELOCITY` — trainer applied to ≥5 *other* requests in the last 24h. - `EMPTY_PROFILE` — trainer has no headline / bio. - `NEW_ACCOUNT` — trainer account is younger than 24h at apply time. - `TEMPLATE_ANSWERS` — identical canonical-JSON answer payload found on another application by the same trainer (key-order normalized so it catches copy-paste regardless of client serialization). - `OVER_BUDGET` — proposed rate is more than `3×` the request's `budgetMax`. - `UNVERIFIED_EMAIL` — trainer email is not yet verified. - Score is bucketed at write time: `<30` LOW · `30–59` MEDIUM · `60–89` HIGH · `≥90` CRITICAL. Persisted on `Application.{riskScore, riskLevel, riskFlags, riskComputedAt}` (new columns + new `RiskLevel` enum, migration `20260610000000_t9d_application_risk_signals`). - Scoring is fire-and-forget after the apply commits — it never delays the trainer's response and never returns 5xx if the heuristic fails (`scoreApplication` swallows + logs, `scoreApplicationOrThrow` is the strict admin-rescore path). - Admin surface (`/api/admin/fraud/*`, gated by `ADMIN_ROLE_GROUPS.MODERATION`): list flagged applications by level, mark reviewed (with optional note + `riskReviewedBy` stamp), clear review, force re-score. - Admin UI page at `/admin/fraud` mirrors the existing `/admin/disputes` admin pattern (server component → server actions → `revalidatePath`); appears in admin nav for `SUPER_ADMIN / ADMIN / MODERATOR`. ### What it does NOT do - No automatic action on flagged applications — the admin reviews and decides. Status / contracts / payouts are untouched. - No machine-learning model. Rules-based only; tunable from the source. - No external lookups (no API calls to fraud-detection vendors, no IP / device fingerprinting). The signals are all derived from data already in the DB. ### Files of note - `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` — `Application` gains 7 risk columns + `RiskLevel` enum + `(riskLevel, riskReviewedAt)` composite index for the admin inbox. - `apps/api/src/fraud/fraud.service.ts` — heuristic engine + admin list / review / clear / rescore methods. - `apps/api/src/fraud/admin-fraud.controller.ts` — `GET /admin/fraud/applications`, `POST /admin/fraud/applications/:id/rescore`, `POST/DELETE /admin/fraud/applications/:id/review`. - `apps/api/src/applications/applications.service.ts` — kicks `scoreApplication` after commit (best-effort). - `apps/web/src/app/[locale]/admin/fraud/{page,review-actions,actions}.tsx` — admin UI (server component + server actions + thin client buttons). - `apps/web/src/messages/{en,ar,fr,es}.json` — `admin.fraud.*` namespace + `admin.nav.fraud`. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Verify the migration applies cleanly on a populated DB (`pnpm --filter @trainova/db run prisma:migrate`). Existing rows will have `riskScore=NULL`; the admin page hides them by default and the "Re-score" button populates them on demand. - [ ] Sanity-check the disposable-email list against any real users you care about — none of the curated 50 domains overlap with mainstream providers, but if your seed data uses `+test@trainova.ai` style aliases they're fine. - [ ] Tune the thresholds (`VELOCITY_LIMIT`, `NEW_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_MS`, `OVER_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER`, signal weights) in `fraud.service.ts` to your traffic. The defaults are conservative: a brand-new trainer with an empty profile applying to 6 jobs in a day with a 4× over-budget rate maxes out at HIGH (75), not CRITICAL. - [ ] Skim `/admin/fraud` as a `MODERATOR` and verify nav link visibility, filter chips, mark-reviewed flow, and re-score button. ### Notes - `TEMPLATE_ANSWERS` only checks within the same trainer (catches one trainer reusing the same essay across many applications); cross-trainer template detection is a separate signal we can layer on later if needed. - `OVER_BUDGET` deliberately requires *both* sides to have numbers — a missing `budgetMax` (company opted out of a ceiling) or a missing `proposedRate` is not suspicious. - Admin role gating uses the existing `ADMIN_ROLE_GROUPS.MODERATION` set (SUPER_ADMIN / ADMIN / MODERATOR). FINANCE / CONTENT / ADS roles do not see the fraud surface — risk review is moderation, not finance. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c9d231edabbe4b2e9d4a8e0704df9636 Requested by: @mohammed3001 ---

### Motivation
- The CLI first-run experience produced scaffolded projects with stale/invalid dependency hints and placeholder tests that did not reliably build in-repo.
- `adze parse` previously printed vague messages for unimplemented paths and could mislead users into thinking full parsing was available from the CLI.
- The goal was to make `adze init` produce a buildable starter crate and make parse-related commands truthful and testable.

### Description
- `adze init` now generates dependency specs that prefer local workspace path dependencies when the CLI was built from a source checkout and otherwise use the current `adze-cli` package version, via a new helper `scaffold_dependency_specs`.  (changes in `cli/src/main.rs`).
- The generated `Cargo.toml` now includes a `pure-rust` feature stub so the scaffolded `build.rs` can use the pure-Rust parser generation path, and the generated `build.rs` remains `build_parsers("src/grammar.rs")`.
- Grammar scaffolding was fixed to avoid an empty-start rule by setting `#[adze::repeat(non_empty = true)]` for the `Program` root and to sanitize project names into identifier-safe grammar names (e.g. `my-lang` -> `my_lang`) via `sanitize_grammar_name`.
- Replaced the placeholder Insta snapshot test in the generated project with a minimal parser smoke test that initializes the generated language and asserts a root node is produced for a minimal input.
- `adze parse` now bails with explicit, user-friendly error messages for unimplemented/experimental modes: static parse mode reports that it is experimental/unimplemented, and dynamic parse mode reports experimental/incomplete status (and errors if the `dynamic` feature is unavailable); `parse_file_dynamic` also returns a clear message rather than silently printing success.
- Added CLI integration tests to cover the improved first-run path: `test_init_generates_buildable_project`, `test_parse_static_mode_reports_unimplemented_behavior`, and `test_init_sanitizes_grammar_name_for_non_identifier_project_names` (changes in `cli/tests/cli_test.rs`).

### Testing
- Ran `cargo fmt --all --check` which succeeded.
- Ran `cargo test -p adze-cli -- --nocapture` which completed: new/updated CLI unit and integration tests passed, with output showing all CLI tests succeeding.
- The `init` scaffold was exercised by a test that creates a temporary project and runs `cargo check` inside it to validate the generated crate is buildable (test passed in CI-local run).

author: alazi900-coder
body:
## Summary

فحصت المشروع سطراً سطراً ووجدت أن **خط أنابيب الترجمة الحالي معطّل في معظم الحالات** — الواجهة الخلفية كانت تُمرّر كل أنواع الملفات عبر `smartChunk` نفسها، فلم تُستدعَ معالجات JSON / SRT / Xenoblade الموجودة في المشروع أصلاً. هذا الـ PR يصلح ذلك ويضيف عدة ميزات.

### إصلاحات أساسية

- **خط أنابيب موحّد جديد** (`server/translationPipeline.ts`) يكتشف نوع الملف ويختار المعالج المناسب: `json` / `json_xenoblade` / `srt` / `txt` / `epub` / `docx`.
- **حفاظ على بنية الملفات الناتجة**:
  - SRT يُعاد بناؤها مع توقيتاتها الأصلية.
  - JSON يُعاد بناؤها مع الحفاظ على الهيكل والمفاتيح التقنية.
  - Xenoblade JSON تستعيد علامات `[XENO:...]` و `[System:...]` و `[ML:...]` عبر تطابق المسار (path-based) بدل تطابق النص.
- **معالجة متوازية مع إعادة محاولة**: ترجمة الأجزاء بشكل متوازٍ (concurrency قابل للضبط، 4 افتراضياً) مع backoff أُسي عند الفشل بدلاً من الاستبدال الصامت بالنص الأصلي.
- إصلاح خطأ `tsc --noEmit` في `server/_core/storageProxy.ts` (فهرسة `req.params[0]`).

### ميزات جديدة

- **تفعيل `XenobladeSettings` المعطّل سابقاً** ودمجه في الصفحة الرئيسية. الإعدادات تُحفظ في `localStorage` (`preserveXenoTags` / `System` / `ML` / `excludeJapanese` / `chunkSize`) وتُرسل إلى الخادم.
- إضافة **JSON** إلى الصيغ المدعومة، مع **اكتشاف Xenoblade JSON تلقائياً** عبر مفاتيح `bdat-bin:` أو وجود علامات `[XENO:` / `[System:` / `[ML:`.
- **منتقي لغات قابل للبحث** (cmdk + popover) يدعم 30+ لغة بالاسم العربي والإنجليزي ورمز ISO.
- **زر تبديل الثيم** (داكن/فاتح) موصول بـ `ThemeProvider`؛ الافتراضي الآن داكن ليتطابق مع التصميم.
- إجراءات tRPC جديدة: `translation.download` (يعيد signed URL) و `translation.stats`.
- في `TranslationHistory`: استخدام الروابط الموقّعة للتنزيل، البحث على أسماء اللغات الكاملة (وليس الرموز فقط)، عرض اسم اللغة في tooltip.
- التحقق من حجم الملف (حدّ 25MB) والصيغ المدعومة على العميل مع `toast` للنجاح والفشل.

### تحسينات الجودة

- **برومبت نظام محسّن** للترجمة يحفظ المتغيرات والعلامات والأرقام وأسطر التنسيق.
- **تنظيف `TECHNICAL_KEYS`** في `jsonProcessor.ts`: القائمة السابقة كانت تستبعد مفاتيح شائعة مثل `value` و `text` التي تحوي نصوصاً قابلة للترجمة فعلياً، وكانت بها مفاتيح مكررة (`interface`, `default`).
- **اختبارات وحدة جديدة** لـ `translationPipeline` و `jsonProcessor` و `xenobladeProcessor`. النتائج: 25 اختباراً ينجحون جميعاً.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] رفع ملف **JSON من Xenoblade Chronicles فعلي** والتحقق من ترجمة النصوص مع بقاء كل العلامات `[XENO:...]` و `[System:Color]` و `[ML:icon]` في مواقعها وعدم ترجمة المفاتيح التقنية مثل `bdat-bin:bdat_common_ms`.
- [ ] رفع ملف **SRT** والتحقق من ظهور الترجمة في الناتج مع الحفاظ على التوقيتات الأصلية في كل سطر.
- [ ] رفع ملف **JSON عام** (غير Xenoblade) والتحقق من إعادة بناء الهيكل بشكل صحيح وعدم ترجمة `id` / `url` / `uuid` / المفاتيح التقنية الأخرى.
- [ ] التحقق من أن **زر تبديل الثيم** يعمل ويُحفظ في `localStorage`.
- [ ] فتح **الإعدادات المتقدمة** في الصفحة الرئيسية، تغيير `chunkSize` إلى قيمة صغيرة (مثلاً 200) وملاحظة أن الترجمة تُقسّم إلى عدد أكبر من الأجزاء وتسير أبطأ ولكن أكثر دقة.
- [ ] في صفحة **السجل**، الضغط على زر التنزيل والتأكد من أن الرابط الموقّع يفتح ملف الترجمة مباشرةً.

### Test Plan

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm check` — يجب أن ينجح (كان يفشل قبل هذا الـ PR).
3. `pnpm test` — يجب أن تنجح 25 حالة.
4. `pnpm dev` ثم زيارة `/` وتجربة رفع كل صيغة (TXT, SRT, JSON عام, Xenoblade JSON, EPUB, DOCX) ومراقبة الناتج في `/history` ثم تنزيله.
5. تجربة تبديل الثيم وتجربة منتقي اللغة بالبحث.

### Notes

- لم أحدّث الـ migrations أو الـ schema (لا حاجة لتغيير قاعدة البيانات).
- ملف `server/fileProcessors.ts` لم يتغيّر منطقياً — `processJsonFile` هناك أصبح غير مستخدم بعد إضافة الـ pipeline الجديد، لكنني أبقيته كما هو لتجنّب كسر أي كود خارجي محتمل. يمكن إزالته لاحقاً.
- التغييرات لا تُعدّل قاعدة البيانات؛ السجلات الموجودة قبل الـ PR تبقى متوافقة.
- التركيز كان على إصلاحات سلوكية وميزات؛ تركت ملفات لم ألمس منطقها بدون تنسيق pretty لتقليل ضوضاء الـ diff.

author: ljchang
body:
Found while testing v0.1.0a5 on dartbrains. The AST scanner only recognised \`mo.ui.slider(start, stop, step=N)\` (positional start/stop) and missed \`mo.ui.slider(start=A, stop=B, step=N)\` — marimo's own recommended style and what dartbrains uses everywhere.

Refactored \`_slider_values\` to delegate to a new \`_resolve_slider_bounds\` helper that fills start/stop/step from any combination of positional + kwarg arguments. The continuous-slider opt-out rule still applies: both stop AND step must be present (positional or kwarg) for a candidate to register; missing step → continuous → render static.

## Tests (4 new, 102/102 passing)

- all-kwargs basic (\`start=A, stop=B, step=N\`)
- all-kwargs no step → continuous
- all-kwargs with \`value=\` default
- dartbrains-style with extra kwargs (\`label=\"...\"\`)

## Real-world signal

Without this fix, *every* dartbrains slider would have been silently ignored by the precompute scanner — the warnings I added in v0.1.0a5 (\"X widgets found, v1 supports single-widget pages only\") would never have fired for those pages. dartbrains would have shown precompute as broken-by-omission rather than with a clear v1-limitation explanation.

author: mizzy
body:
## Summary

The pest grammar accepted `use_expr` in any primary-value position, but the evaluator only handled it as the RHS of a top-level `let` binding. The mismatch produced silent failures (e.g. `use { ... }` inside a list became a literal string; inside an if branch it was misparsed as a `module_call` named "use").

This PR implements direction 1 from #2233 (tighten the grammar to match the evaluator):

- `let_binding`'s RHS now allows `(use_expr | expression)`. `use_expr` is the only meta-statement allowed there.
- Remove `use_expr` from `primary`.
- `module_call` gains a `!use_keyword` guard so `use { ... }` cannot silently parse as a module call named "use" now that `use_expr` is no longer ahead of it in `primary`.
- Mirror the same shape in the formatter grammar (`carina_fmt.pest`) so the `pest_grammar_parity` invariant holds.
- Drop the now-unreachable `Rule::use_expr` arm from `parse_primary_with_resource_or_module`; handle it directly in `parse_let_binding_extended`.

## Why direction 1, not 2 or 3

- Direction 2 (`Value::Module`, modules-as-first-class-values) would be a much bigger design change with implications for module resolution, exports, and the resolver. There is no current roadmap need for dynamic module selection.
- Direction 3 (keep grammar drift, emit a runtime error) just pushes an error that can be a parse error down to runtime. Direction 1 is strictly better.
- Direction 1 is reversible: if `Value::Module` is wanted later, loosening the grammar is easy.

## Test plan

- [x] Added 4 new parser tests covering the four positions named in the issue (module-call argument, list element, if branch, local-let RHS). All Red → Green confirmed.
- [x] `cargo test` (full workspace) — all PASS
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — no warnings
- [x] `cargo build` — succeeds
- [x] Real-infra smoke test: `carina validate infra/aws/management/github-oidc/` still passes (`let X = use { ... }` still works)
- [x] Existing `nested_modules` and `module_list` fixtures continue to pass

Closes #2233

author: sarah-allec
body:
## Summary

Adds end-to-end HPC integration to SciLink's Streamlit UI: Users can connect to
a remote cluster from the sidebar, generate simulation inputs via AI agents,
submit jobs, monitor status, and retrieve results — all without leaving the
browser.

## New: `scilink/hpc/` module

A provider-agnostic HPC backend built on Paramiko:

- **`HPCConnection`** — Thread-safe SSH client with SFTP helpers (`upload`,
  `download`, `read_text`, `mkdir_p`, …). Resolves all IPs for a hostname and
  fails over automatically. Supports password auth, SSH keys, and `ProxyJump`
  for bastion hosts.
- **`HPCProfile`** — Lightweight dataclass for saveable connection profiles
  (no secrets stored).
- **`Scheduler`** abstract base with concrete implementations for:
  | Scheduler | Submit | Status | Queue | Partitions |
  |-----------|--------|--------|-------|------------|
  | **SLURM** | `sbatch` | `scontrol` → `sacct` fallback | `squeue` | `sinfo` |
  | **PBS/Torque** | `qsub` | `qstat -f` | `qstat` | `qstat -Q` |
  | **LSF** | `bsub` | `bjobs` | `bjobs` | `bqueues` |
- **`detect_scheduler(conn)`** — Probes the remote host and returns the first
  matching scheduler instance.

## Changed: Sidebar (`sidebar.py`)

- New **HPC Connection** expander with:
  - Login form (host, user, port, auth method, key path, proxy jump)
  - Saved profile selector (persisted in `session_state`)
  - Auto-detection of scheduler on connect
  - Live status: `🟢 user@host`, scheduler name, active job count

author: slepp
body:
Closes #1419

`hew_cron_next` and `hew_cron_next_n` previously used in-band sentinel return values to conflate success, no-next-occurrence, null/invalid input, and invalid epoch handling.

This change moves the timestamp payload to out data, returns explicit status codes for each outcome class, and exposes `hew_cron_last_error` to carry thread-local diagnostic detail. Hew-side wrappers now preserve the existing surface method while adding structured `try_next` error handling.

### Compatibility
FFI signature change. Hew-side wrappers in `std/time/cron/cron.hew` updated; surface `next()` remains available.

### Validation
- `cargo test -p hew-std-time-cron --quiet`
- `cargo clippy -p hew-std-time-cron --tests -- -D warnings`
- `make ci-preflight`
- `make test-hew`

### Note
The upstream `cron` crate currently constrains parsed years to 1970..=2100, so the regression test verifies that success can carry a payload of `-1` without sentinel collision at the ABI level while distinct status codes cover each failure class.

author: keli-wen
body:
## Summary

Lands `quantmind/knowledge/` as a **data standard with three shapes** plus the `quantmind/configs/` skeleton. The knowledge schema is the contract every downstream module (flows, utils, retrieval, future `KnowledgeStore`) builds on; this PR ships schema only — the storage layer is specified but lands separately.

### `quantmind/knowledge/` — three-shape data standard

- **`BaseKnowledge`** — root for every shape. Carries `id` (auto UUID), `item_type`, `schema_version`, `as_of` (mandatory), `created_at`, `source: SourceRef` (typed provenance — no bare strings), `extraction: ExtractionRef | None`, `confidence`, `citations`, `tags`, `disclaimers`, plus an `embedding_text()` contract that subclasses MUST override so the future store knows what to embed.
- **`FlattenKnowledge`** — atomic-card shape. Subclasses: `News`, `Earnings`, `PaperKnowledgeCard`.
- **`TreeKnowledge`** — hierarchical-artifact shape. Holds `root_node_id` plus a flat `nodes: dict[UUID, TreeNode]` map. Helpers: `root()`, `children_of()`, `walk_dfs()`, `find_path()`. Default `embedding_text()` delegates to root. Subclass: `Paper` (whole paper as section tree).
- **`GraphKnowledge`** — placeholder. The class exists for type-hinting `BaseKnowledge | FlattenKnowledge | TreeKnowledge | GraphKnowledge`, but `__init_subclass__` raises `NotImplementedError` until the shape is finalised in a later PR.

`Citation` gains optional `tree_id` / `node_id` anchors for tree-rooted citations. The full design rationale (PageIndex-style navigation, embedding as pre-filter not replacement, future SQLite + `sqlite-vec` backend, Python-interface contract for `KnowledgeStore`) is captured in the local design spec.

### `quantmind/configs/`

Unchanged from the original PR3: `BaseFlowCfg` + `BaseInput` plus per-flow `<Name>FlowCfg` and `<Name>Input` discriminated unions for paper / news / earnings.

### Other changes

- `openai-agents>=0.14` added as a hard dep so `BaseFlowCfg.model_settings: ModelSettings | None` is honoured.
- `import-linter` contracts: `knowledge` is a leaf; `configs` may only depend on `knowledge`.
- `quantmind/config/registry._discover_flows_in_path` made resilient to `OSError` from `Path.rglob` (transitional code; deleted in PR5).
- `basedpyright`'s `reportIncompatibleVariableOverride` disabled so the Pydantic v2 idiom of narrowing a `str` field to `Literal[...]` in subclasses (used throughout the discriminator pattern) does not produce spurious errors.

Old `quantmind/models/{content,paper,analysis}.py` and `quantmind/config/*` stay in place; transitional `parsers/`, `sources/`, `flow/`, `llm/` still depend on them and they get deleted in PR4-PR5.

Part of #71.

- [ ] CI verify workflow green on the PR
- [ ] `python -c "from quantmind.knowledge import Paper, PaperKnowledgeCard, News, Earnings, FlattenKnowledge, TreeKnowledge, GraphKnowledge; print('OK')"` prints `OK`

body:
## Summary

Promotes the scripts primitive from `dev` to `main`. Scripts are a new artifact kind alongside Workflows (`kind: "script"`): stateless, fetch-only Cloudflare Workers built from the same canvas and node graph but compiled to `export default { fetch }` instead of a `WorkflowEntrypoint` class.

- **Single graph, two artifact kinds.** Workflows and scripts share the node graph; codegen dispatches on `ir.kind`. Scripts reject `sleep`/`sleep_until`/`wait_for_event` (no durable runtime), have no `WORKFLOW` self-binding, and have no instance lifecycle.
- **Back-compat preserved.** `kind` on `WorkflowIR` is optional; legacy stored IRs without the discriminator continue to validate as workflows. DB column defaults to `'workflow'` for existing rows.
- **`EXPORT_` prefix convention.** A node display-named `EXPORT_X` surfaces on `graph.X` in the script's response; unexported, unreferenced nodes get their `const` decl dropped to keep generated code lean.
- **UI surface as "Function (Beta)"** in the New dropdown; canvas filters incompatible nodes; editor shows a Function badge; deploy page messaging adapts.
- **Docs** updated across both the internal API reference (`docs/api-reference.md`) and the public VitePress site (`apps/docs/`) — homepage, architecture, workflow-ir, compilation, run-lifecycle, REST API, IR schema, triggers, and sidebar.

17 commits ahead of `main`. release-please will compute the version bump from the conventional-commit prefixes (multiple `feat:` → minor bump).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `pnpm test` / `pnpm build` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm type-check` all green on `dev` HEAD
- [ ] Smoke: create a Workflow on prod-like → save → deploy → trigger → run completes (regression guard for the existing path)
- [ ] Smoke: create a Function from "New → Function (Beta)" → save → deploy → POST to deployed Worker URL with a JSON body → response is `Response.json(graph)` shaped by `EXPORT_`-prefixed nodes
- [ ] Validation: drop a `sleep` / `sleep_until` / `wait_for_event` into a Function canvas → publish-time error blocks deploy
- [ ] API contract: `POST /workflows/:id/trigger` against a deployed Function returns 400
- [ ] Back-compat: an existing pre-release workflow (no `kind` field in stored IR) loads, edits, deploys, and runs unchanged
- [ ] Wrangler shape: Function's `wrangler.json` has no `[[workflows]]` table and no `WORKFLOW` binding; Workflow's still does
- [ ] Local dev works for both kinds
- [ ] DB migration: `ALTER TABLE workflows ADD COLUMN kind text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'workflow'` runs cleanly on prod-like data
- [ ] Public docs render correctly — Workflows-vs-Functions sidebar entries land on the right anchors

author: jspanos
body:
## Summary
- Adds a new wire-protocol message `NOTICE` (server → client, fire-and-forget) so the relay can stream informational messages to a connected client without a client release.
- Bumps `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1.2 → 1.3 (additive, backward compatible — old clients ignore unknown types).
- Reorders install docs to **curl → pipx → brew** to match hle.world docs.

## Why
Today, dashboard-side state (e.g. *Auto-protect new tunnels*) is applied silently and the CLI never tells the user their tunnel is SSO-gated. With `NOTICE`, the server controls wording — adding a new message type does not require shipping a new client.

## Technical details
- `hle_common/protocol.py`: new `MessageType.NOTICE`, new `NoticePayload` (`level: info|success|warning|error`, `code`, `message`, optional `details`, optional `url`).
- `hle_client/notices.py` (new): renders a `NoticePayload` to stderr via rich, with level glyphs (`ℹ ✓ ⚠ ✗`).
- `hle_client/tunnel.py`: adds a `NOTICE` case in the receive loop. Malformed payloads are logged and dropped.
- Tests: `test_protocol.py::TestNoticePayload`, new `test_notices.py` covers all levels, URL rendering, and unknown-level fallback (forward compatible if the server adds new levels).
- README install section reordered: curl one-liner is the primary path; pipx and Homebrew listed as alternatives.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/`
- [ ] After merge: bump submodule pointer in the server repo and wire up emission sites (auto-auth applied, settings changed).

author: penta2himajin
body:
## Summary

Mirrors PR #11's ja swap, this time for **English**. Replaces `whisper-tiny.en` with `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3` for the L1 `en` path.

| Metric | whisper-tiny.en | parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| WER | 8.37% | **7.53%** | −10% relative |
| RTF (warm) | 0.10 | **0.05** | −50% |
| ASR p50 | 853 ms | **534 ms** | −37% |

en + ja are now both on Parakeet; zh remains on whisper-tiny pending a separate evaluation (research summary in the side notes — recommended next swap is **Belle-whisper-large-v3-zh** through the existing whisper.cpp adapter).

## How it works

1. **No new fork patch.** `ParakeetAdapter::load(dir)` (without `_with_feature_size`) is already correct for v3 — default 128-mel preprocessor matches what `istupakov/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-onnx` exports. The existing fork pin from PR #11 covers both 80-mel (ja) and 128-mel (en) usage.

2. **`eval_l1_smoke` gains `--parakeet-en-dir`** (also via `PARAKEET_EN_DIR`). Same cfg-gating pattern as `--parakeet-ja-dir`. When omitted, falls back to whisper-tiny.en.

3. **`build_pipeline` adds an `"en" if parakeet_en_dir.is_some()` branch** that calls `ParakeetAdapter::load(dir)`. Whisper fallback unchanged.

4. **`asr_model` baseline label** is now formatted dynamically:
   ```
   "<ggml-tiny.en|parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3> (en) /
    <ggml-tiny|parakeet-tdt_ctc-0.6b-ja> (ja) / ggml-tiny (zh)"
   ```

## What lands

- `examples/eval_l1_smoke.rs` — `--parakeet-en-dir` flag, en branch in `build_pipeline`, dynamic asr_model label
- `scripts/setup_parakeet_en.sh` — downloads from `istupakov/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-onnx` (~2.4 GB FP32; optional `PARAKEET_EN_QUANTIZED=1` for ~622 MB int8 — **FP32 default because int8 noticeably regressed WER** to ~25% in side-by-side testing)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — parallel cache+download step for `vendor/parakeet_en`
- `docs/benchmarks/ci_baseline.json` — regenerated with both parakeet paths
- `docs/spec.md` §3.1 — ParakeetAdapter en bullet promoted to current default
- `docs/evaluation.md` §1.1 — L1 description reflects en+ja parakeet, zh whisper
- `README.md` — adds `setup_parakeet_en.sh` to the script index

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --all-targets --locked` — 125 tests, all green
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --features onnx --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Local end-to-end with both `--parakeet-en-dir` and `--parakeet-ja-dir`:
  - `[en] WER=0.0753 RTF=0.32` (parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3, 128-mel)
  - `[ja] CER=0.0331 RTF=0.28` (parakeet-tdt_ctc-0.6b-ja, 80-mel)
  - `[zh] CER=0.3231 RTF=0.14` (whisper-tiny multilingual)
- [x] CI on this PR passes (4 jobs; `evaluate-asr` will see ~5 min cold-cache parakeet-en download on first run)

## Risks

- **Cold cache adds ~5 min for the 2.4 GB en encoder**. Warm cache adds ~10 s. Total CI cost: similar pattern to PR #11.
- **GitHub Actions cache pressure**: now ~9 GB total (whisper.cpp 200 MB + parakeet ja 2.4 GB + parakeet en 2.4 GB + Rust target 3-4 GB + FLEURS subset 30 MB). Comfortably under the 10 GB per-repo limit.
- **First-inference cold-start spike** (~14 s) lands in p95 latency, not p50. Absolute warn checks are p50-only so cold-start doesn't fire false positives.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- **zh swap** — research summary at the bottom of the commit message. Recommended near-term: Belle-whisper-large-v3-zh through the existing whisper.cpp adapter (Apache-2.0, drops zh CER from 32% to single digits, no new code path)
- ort-native zh: SenseVoice-Small is the strongest candidate but its model license needs commercial-use verification first
- Moonshine-zh tested but accuracy too low (~25% FLEURS-zh, barely better than whisper-tiny)
